definitions.explanation: A class of biological molecules — DNA and RNA — that carry genetic information in all living organisms. Essential to the fields of genetics, molecular biology, and biotechnology.

examples.english: There are two types of nucleic acid: DNA and RNA.

examples.japanese: {核酸|かくさん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{遺伝|いでん}{情報|じょうほう}→遺伝情報：26494_idenjouhou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|にな}う→担う：12787_ninau⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧な⟦{物質|ぶっしつ}→物質：03608_busshitsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Nucleic acids are important substances that carry genetic information.

examples.japanese: ⟦ウイルス→ウイルス：05223_uirusu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{核酸|かくさん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{検出|けんしゅつ}→検出：13132_kenshutsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧PCR{検査|けんさ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{感染症|かんせんしょう}→感染症：15681_kansenshou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{診断|しんだん}→診断：04209_shindan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{使|つか}われている→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: PCR testing, which detects viral nucleic acids, is widely used for diagnosing infectious diseases.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{核|かく}→核：13127_kaku⟧ (nucleus, core) and ⟦{酸|さん}→酸：28620_san⟧ (acid). So named because nucleic acids were first isolated from cell nuclei. The term became widely known to the general public through PCR testing during the COVID-19 pandemic, where "nucleic acid testing" ({核酸|かくさん}⟦{検査|けんさ}→検査：02707_kensa⟧) became a household phrase in Japan.

Note: the homophone ⟦{拡散|かくさん}→拡散：08178_kakusan⟧ (spread, diffusion) is a completely different word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {核酸|かくさん}⟦{検査|けんさ}→検査：02707_kensa⟧: nucleic acid test (PCR test)
- {核酸|かくさん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{構造|こうぞう}→構造：02730_kouzou⟧: structure of nucleic acids
- {核酸|かくさん}⟦{医薬品|いやくひん}→医薬品：19711_iyakuhin⟧: nucleic acid therapeutics
- {核酸|かくさん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抽出|ちゅうしゅつ}する→抽出する：19627_chuushutsusuru⟧: to extract nucleic acids

RELATED WORDS:
- DNA (ディーエヌエー): deoxyribonucleic acid — one of the two types of nucleic acid
- RNA (アールエヌエー): ribonucleic acid — the other type of nucleic acid
- ⟦{遺伝子|いでんし}→遺伝子：05031_idenshi⟧: gene — a functional unit of nucleic acid
- {塩基|えんき}: base (chemistry) — the building blocks of nucleic acid sequences
